questions.q: In the context of ComfyUI's execution graph, what is the primary purpose of topological sorting?
options: To minimize the memory usage of the cache
To determine the strict order in which nodes must be executed based on dependencies
To validate that all data types match between connected nodes
To clear the cache when a model file is changed on disk
questions.answer: To determine the strict order in which nodes must be executed based on dependencies
questions.why: The lesson states that topological sorting is used to find a strict order where tasks with no prerequisites are done first, unlocking subsequent layers, ensuring that a node only runs after its inputs are ready.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what happens to the cache for a node's descendants when that node's input changes (e.g., a new seed is set)?
options: The entire cache is cleared immediately
The cache for the changed node and all its descendants is invalidated (marked as dirty)
The cache for the changed node is kept, but descendants are recalculated
The cache is only invalidated if the model file on disk is also changed
questions.answer: The cache for the changed node and all its descendants is invalidated (marked as dirty)
questions.why: The 'Invalidation' section explains that when a node changes, the engine must invalidate the cache for that node and all its descendants (Desc(x)) because their input signatures have changed.

questions.q: Which file in the `comfy_execution` folder contains the `TopologicalSort` and `ExecutionList` classes?
options: comfy_execution/caching.py
comfy_execution/validation.py
comfy_execution/graph.py
comfy_execution/progress.py
questions.why: The 'In ComfyUI' section explicitly lists `comfy_execution/graph.py` as containing `TopologicalSort` and `ExecutionList`.

questions.q: In the Lab simulation, why was the recompute count 6 after changing the value of node B, instead of 7?
options: Node A was skipped because its inputs did not change, so only B and its descendants were recalculated
Node G was skipped because it was already cached from the previous run
The engine failed to detect the change in B, so it only ran the remaining nodes
Nodes C and D were skipped because they are constants
questions.answer: Node A was skipped because its inputs did not change, so only B and its descendants were recalculated
questions.why: The Lab results explain that changing B meant the engine did not recompute A (since A's inputs were unchanged). It only recomputed B and its descendants (C, D, E, F, G), totaling 6 nodes.

questions.q: What is the consequence of creating a loop (cycle) in a ComfyUI workflow graph?
options: The graph will execute in an infinite loop until manually stopped
The `validate_loops` function will reject the graph, preventing execution
The cache will be automatically cleared to prevent data corruption
The topological sort will randomly select an order to break the cycle
questions.answer: The `validate_loops` function will reject the graph, preventing execution
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section states that ComfyUI will reject the graph if `validate_loops` finds a cycle, as cycles are invalid in a standard execution graph.
